title: Operator handoff micro-illustrations and inline CLI snapshot kit for Private Network first-run
creator: Leah Moreno
description:
Objective: Produce a small, high-clarity asset bundle for operator-first touch during Private/VPC first-run and upgrades. The kit is focused on the operator persona who performs initial network handshakes, CLI bootstrap, and in-place upgrades. Deliverables must be lightweight to embed in docs, the Console quickstart modal, and in support runbooks.

Goals:
- Reduce confusion during the first infrastructure handshake: show exactly where to check connectivity, KMS key state, and service account permissions.
- Provide a single set of micro-illustrations (static SVGs + one animated handshake GIF) that scale to inline docs and the Console header.
- Provide 5 annotated screenshots (desktop + mobile variants) of the installer/upgrade UI with redlines and copy variants for localization.
- Include a set of inline CLI snapshot images for the most common operator commands (bootstrap, rotate-keys, health-check). These should include terminal highlight overlays and suggested follow-up checks.

Scope and constraints:
- Visual style follows the current Redwood brand tokens but uses a simplified palette to avoid heavy contrast in console dark mode.
- Assets must be accessible: SVGs with descriptive title/desc, text at 14px legible baseline, and color contrast >= 4.5:1 for all callouts.
- Avoid duplicating the larger onboarding illustration packs; this is intentionally minimal and task-focused. Do not reuse previously created multi-step storyboards word-for-word.

Deliverables (explicit):
1) Micro-illustration set (4 SVGs):
   - 'Handshake' (network + token exchange) static with animated GIF variant for docs landing page.
   - 'KMS check' (key + padlock iconography).
   - 'CIDR verification' (diagram of permitted ranges + tooltip pointer).
   - 'Upgrade safe-state' (server + progress bar + fallback toggle).
2) Annotated screenshots (5 flows x 2 viewports):
   - Installer first-run: connection test, credentials input, result states.
   - Upgrade flow: preview changes, migration progress, rollback affordance.
   - CLI snapshot overlays for bootstrap, rotate-keys, health-check. Each screenshot must include short microcopy variants (primary, concise, verbose) for A/B testing.
3) Redline sheet (PDF) with spacing, color swatches, export sizes, and accessibility notes.
4) Figma file (hand-off) with component tokens and slice exports named for the repo.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma file is review-ready with component tokens and marked slices for engineering export.
- QA: Visual review passed by PM and Eng (visual pass + successful manual validation of CLI examples by an engineer).
- Localization: copy variants prepared and flagged for translation; no hard-coded text in embedded images (use overlays where possible).
- Security sign-off: review of KMS-related language by security team (see dependency).

Notes on approach and trade-offs:
- Chose micro-illustrations over full storyboards to keep assets maintainable and re-usable across docs and console UI.
- GIF animation limited to a single handshake loop to reduce file size and distraction in docs pages.
- Selected terminal snapshot approach (static image + highlight overlays) rather than live terminal embeds to avoid exposing runtime secrets in screenshots and to keep docs static-cache friendly.

Handoff instructions for engineering:
- Export two SVG sizes: 320px width (inline docs), 720px width (console header).
- Provide one GIF at max 800px by 200px, optimized for web (lossy, under 200KB).
- Provide PNGs for screenshots (2x scaling for retina) and a JPG small for thumbnails.
- Add figma export naming convention: DES-831234_<asset_name>_<size>

References and links:
- PRD: https://docs.redwood.ai/private-onboard/prd-operator-slim-kit (internal)
- Figma placeholder: https://www.figma.com/file/PrivateOnboard/Operator-Mini-Kit (will be created under design/team files)
- GitHub PR (design notes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4123

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Engineers need different screenshot crops for hosted vs private console. Mitigation: provide viewport-safe slices and a PSD/figma frame for quick recrops.
- Risk: Security copy is sensitive around key rotation. Mitigation: include a clearly marked callout and route final language to Security reviewer (dependency ENG-40212).
